Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we had a good internal alignment. Procurement asked me to push ahead with the Order Form and the MSA redlines, and we have two security-specific asks we need to resolve before we finalize:

1) Pen test / staging access: we need clarity on notice windows (preferred 30 days) and whether testing can be conducted on a tenant-scoped staging environment.
2) Evidence cadence for SOC 2 artifacts (system description, controls mapping, and quarterly evidence snapshots) — our security team needs a predictable delivery schedule and a named contact.

I attached the latest OrderForm (MedCo_OrderForm_v3.pdf). Can you confirm what your typical evidence cadence is and if Redwood can commit to a bounded inspection window (we prefer 2 business days for scheduled access) vs. full onsite inspection language? Also please confirm any constraints for pen-test scope (credentialed vs. non-credentialed, acceptance criteria).

High-level timeline: we’d like final redlines and the updated Order Form by COB next week if possible.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: MedCo order form — audit language & evidence cadence

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear ask and for attaching the Order Form. Looping in Laura (legal) and David (platform engineering) to confirm the technical and contract details. Quick answers up-front:

- Evidence cadence: we can commit to quarterly evidence snapshots for SOC 2 artifacts (submission within 10 business days of quarter close) and a named evidence POC on our side.
- Bounded inspection: we prefer scheduled, tenant-scoped inspection windows. We can do scheduled 2 business-day on-demand access for evidence review (subject to a 30-day notice for pen-test staging access).
- Pen-test scope constraints: we support credentialed pen tests on a customer-scoped staging instance with agreed test hours and a scoped blast radius. We require a pre-test questionnaire and a single point of contact for coordination.

Proposed next steps:
1) Laura to propose MSA clause language for "Inspection & Evidence" and "Penetration Testing" that keeps inspections tenant-scoped and time-boxed.
2) David to confirm operational requirements for a temporary staging instance and the list of logs/artifacts we can provide.
3) Ben/Olga will incorporate the redlines into the Order Form and return for your review by EOD next Friday (2027-08-27).

If the timeline is tight for MedCo, let us know which items are deal-blockers so we can prioritize.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Trust & Security Programs, Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: MedCo redlines — proposed language and ops needs

Team — forwarding MedCo’s asks. I sketched language below that I think keeps the commercial terms moving while protecting our operational constraints. Please review and reply with any blocking concerns.

Suggested contract text (high level):
- Inspection & Audit Rights: "Customer may request scheduled, tenant-scoped inspections limited to production-equivalent staging environments. Redwood will provide access during a 2-business-day scheduled window; requests for inspection must be submitted at least 14 calendar days in advance. Redwood will not permit unrestricted or continuous access to internal systems; any additional requests will be considered on a case-by-case basis and subject to a written agreement."
- Penetration Testing: "Customer may perform a single credentialed penetration test per 12-month period on an agreed staging environment. Tests must be coordinated with Redwood, include a pre-test questionnaire, and agree to limited blast radius rules and emergency contact procedures. Redwood will accept and remediate confirmed severity-1 findings per the SLA attached to the Order Form."
- Evidence Cadence: "Redwood will deliver SOC 2 quarterly evidence snapshots (system description, control mappings, sample artifacts) within 10 business days after quarter close. Evidence will be uploaded to a customer-specific secure Drive folder; ad hoc requests will be triaged to the named evidence POC with a 5-business-day SLA for initial response."

Operational asks for David:
- Confirm that we can provision an ephemeral, customer-scoped staging instance for MedCo and the estimated lead time and costs.
- Confirm what logs/artifacts we can make available for a 2-day inspection window (application logs, audit trails, config snapshots).

Legal asks for Laura:
- Tighten the liability and scope language so we don’t end up with unbounded inspection obligations.
- Approve the 12-month cadence limit on pen tests or propose an alternative.

Ben — can you prepare an initial redlined Order Form that merges Maria’s changes and our suggested text? I’ll circulate a consolidated draft to Maria and Rajiv.

Thanks,
Olga

Subject: Re: Internal: MedCo redlines — proposed language and ops needs

Olga / team — reviewed the suggested language. High level comments and redline guidance below. I attached a tracked doc (redline_MSA.docx) with inline edits.

Key legal points:
- Inspection window: change notice to 21 calendar days (instead of 14) to allow legal/ops coordination and to match typical compliance windows.
- Limitations on data access: add explicit prohibition on exfiltration of production data and require use of a sanitized sample dataset for deeper tests.
- Pen-test frequency: keep to once per 12 months with a carve-out for critical issues that we mutually agree warrant an additional test.
- Remediation & SLAs: require that severity-1 findings trigger our incident response playbook; propose 5 business days for acknowledgement and 30 calendar days for remediation plan delivery.
- Evidence delivery: accept quarterly snapshots, but add confidentiality protections and retention window (retain artifacts for 12 months).

Suggested alternative clause snippet for MSA (for negotiation):
"Customer audit rights shall be time-boxed, tenant-scoped and scheduled. Customer shall provide written notice no less than twenty-one (21) calendar days prior to the requested inspection window. Any penetration testing requires prior written approval, completion of Redwood's pre-test questionnaire and agreement to test scoping constraints. Evidence artifacts provided by Redwood are subject to confidentiality and will be retained for twelve (12) months from delivery."

I also noted a few procurement asks in Maria’s Order Form that are out-of-scope (e.g., requests for full system architecture diagrams). We should push back and provide a sanitized architecture summary instead.

I’ll leave the operational sign-off on provisioning and artifact availability to David. Once he confirms, Ben can produce the redlined Order Form and I’ll finalize the legal doc for Maria to review.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
